extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, NIH staff, and institutional administrators involved in NIH grant review
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of NIH policies, laws, notices, and guidance that govern how grant applications are reviewed, scored, and managed — including integrity/confidentiality, conflict of interest, review criteria, scoring, appeals, and related topic-specific reviewer considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal framework governing NIH peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH peer review is governed by federal Acts and Regulations, including PHS Act 42 U.S.C. 289a (requires two levels of peer review), PHS Act 42 U.S.C. 284a (authorizes scientific and technical peer review through advisory committees), the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), the Government in the Sunshine Act (directing when advisory committee meetings may be closed), and 42 CFR 52h (establishes rules for evaluating applications and conducting peer review meetings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes and regulations define the procedural and legal requirements for how applications must be evaluated, when meetings may be closed, how advisory committees are established/managed, and the requirement for two levels of peer review. See the linked laws/regulations for exact statutory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Integrity and Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and guidance titled 'Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review' and related policy notices (e.g., 'Maintaining Security and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review: Rules, Responsibilities and Possible Consequences' NOT-OD-22-044) set expectations for confidentiality and integrity in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes policy notices and FAQs explaining reviewer responsibilities for maintaining confidentiality, rules for handling proprietary/confidential information, potential consequences for breaches, and case studies illustrating violations and actions. Reviewers must follow these policies to protect application confidentiality and maintain integrity of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of generative artificial intelligence in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technologies is Prohibited for the NIH Peer Review Process (policy notice NOT-OD-23-149).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH reviewers are prohibited from using generative AI tools as part of the peer review process. FAQs provide additional clarification on scope and permitted/unpermitted uses. This prohibition is part of maintaining confidentiality and review integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Conflict of Interest (COI) in NIH peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and notices on managing conflict of interest in the initial peer review of NIH grant and cooperative agreement applications (e.g., Advance Notice: Revised Policy for Managing Conflict of Interest in the Initial Peer Review of NIH Grant and Cooperative Agreement Applications NOT-OD-13-010) and FAQs on Peer Review Conflict of Interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural guidance on identifying and managing COIs for reviewers, policies on recusal, and administrative steps to preserve fairness in review. FAQs and policy notices detail responsibilities and workflows for COI management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Criteria and Considerations / Simplified Review Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Criteria and Considerations and the 'Simplified Review Framework' (e.g., Simplified Review Framework for NIH Research Project Grant Applications NOT-OD-24-010) describe the substantive criteria used to evaluate applications and revisions to review frameworks (including fellowship review changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance for reviewers and applicants on how review criteria are applied, links to reviewer and applicant guidance documents, and FAQs (e.g., 'Review Criteria and Considerations', 'Simplifying Review', 'Revisions to the NIH Fellowship Application and Review Process'). These materials explain evaluation dimensions, how to interpret criteria under the simplified framework, and implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring in First Level Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and notices on scoring procedures in first level peer review, including 'Enhancing Peer Review: The NIH Announces New Scoring Procedures for Evaluation of Research Applications' (NOT-OD-09-024) and related FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how applications are scored in first-level peer review, changes/enhancements to scoring systems, and provides FAQs to explain score interpretation and use in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals in First Level Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals policy and procedures for initial peer review (policy notice NOT-OD-11-064) and applicant guidance such as 'Next Steps'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines when and how applicants may appeal first-level peer review actions, the grounds for appeal, procedural steps, and what applicants can expect after filing an appeal. Linked FAQs and guidance documents provide details for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer guidance and consolidated reviewer documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consolidated List of Reviewer Documents and other reviewer guidance resources provide step-by-step instructions for reviewers on each phase of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains practical instructions for reviewers (how to prepare, submit critiques, score applications), links to required documents, and resources (videos, FAQs). The page points reviewers to the consolidated repository for detailed, stepwise guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Values of NIH Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Core Values of NIH Peer Review' document outlines the foundational principles expected in the review system (e.g., fairness, objectivity, transparency, confidentiality, expertise — as set out in the linked PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as high-level normative guidance for reviewers and NIH staff; reviewers are expected to uphold these values in conducting evaluations. The page links to the PDF and related explanatory material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy/announcement that centralizes peer review of grant applications, cooperative agreements and R&D contracts within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to improve efficiency and strengthen integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes organizational policy intended to standardize and strengthen peer review administration; relevant to understanding how review panels are organized and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial-specific review criteria and human subjects considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Links and guidance on Clinical Trial-Specific Review Criteria, NIH's definition of a clinical trial, decision tools (Is My Project a Clinical Trial?/BESH/Observational study), and Human Subjects in Peer Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides reviewers and applicants with instructions on evaluating human-subjects protections, trial design, and clinical trial-specific criteria. Includes links to required forms, informed consent posting, trial registration/reporting policies, and Good Clinical Practice training expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility expectations for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and guidance for rigor and reproducibility in grant applications (e.g., 'Guidance: Rigor and Reproducibility in Grant Applications', 'Principles and Guidelines for Publishing Preclinical Research').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains expectations for experimental design, transparency, methodological rigor, and reproducibility-related sections in applications. Includes resources and training for applicants and reviewers to implement these expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management & Sharing Policy and review considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Data Management and Sharing Policy guidance, including how to write a Data Management & Sharing Plan, budgeting for data sharing, selecting repositories, and approaches to data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides criteria reviewers may consider regarding data sharing plans and data stewardship. Offers applicant-facing instructions and reviewer resources on evaluating DMS plans and budgeting for data management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomic Data Sharing policy expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Genomic Data Sharing Policy overview and expectations by NIH Institute & Center, including guidance on registration/submission to dbGaP and controlled-access considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for how genomic data should be shared and reviewed; includes contacts and submission instructions for reviewers/applicants dealing with genomic data components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign interference and disclosure of other support/foreign components
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on foreign interference, requirements for disclosure of other support and foreign components, and processes for handling allegations related to foreign interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires disclosure of other support and foreign components, provides processes for handling concerns, and includes resources about obligations and investigative steps. Reviewers and institutions must be aware of these disclosure requirements when assessing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) policies and training
rubrics_metrics.description: FCOI training resources and notices, important highlights of FCOI regulatory requirements (including for foreign institutions) and NIH Guide Notices related to FCOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies training and disclosure obligations for investigators and institutions. Reviewers should consider declared conflicts and institutional compliance; institutions must provide required training and disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Institutional Review Board (sIRB) policy for multi-site research
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and case study material on the use of a single IRB for multi-site or cooperative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains expectations for sIRB use, when it applies, and how reviewers should consider IRB planning and protections when evaluating multi-site human subjects research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and participant protections relevant to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and best practices for protecting participant privacy, designating scientific data for controlled access, considerations for informed consent, and special considerations for working with AI/AN communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides reviewers and applicants on how privacy protections, consent language, and controlled-access designations factor into application review, especially for sensitive or identifiable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct reporting and post-findings actions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policies on research misconduct including definitions, how to report concerns, the process for handling allegations, and NIH expectations/actions/oversight after findings of research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides reviewers and institutions with procedures to report and respond to suspected misconduct, and explains subsequent NIH actions and oversight responsibilities.
